DORSET DIVISION / LEGAL

Accessibility & Complaints

Last updated: 25 October 2026

Accessibility commitment

Dorset Division aims to make this website readable, understandable and usable with keyboards and assistive technology. This is a commitment to improve access, not a claim of a completed independent WCAG certification or full compliance across every page and external service.

Ask for an alternative

If you encounter a barrier, email marnie@dorsetdivision.co.uk or telephone 07342 729185. Please identify the page or task, describe what prevented you using it and tell me what alternative would help. You do not need to provide a diagnosis. I will consider reasonable adjustments and accessible alternatives, such as supplying information in another format or discussing the enquiry directly.

Known limits and third-party services

The website includes large background images, animation and third-party services. Layout, contrast, keyboard focus, zoom and screen-reader behaviour need continuing review. External booking and profile services control their own interfaces. If one prevents you contacting me or accessing information, use the direct contact details above.

Make a service complaint

Please send your name, project reference, a clear account of the concern and the outcome you are seeking. Include relevant dates or supporting information, but do not send passwords or unnecessary sensitive information. You can complain by email, telephone or post using the address in Legal Information.

How I will respond

I aim to acknowledge complaints within two working days and provide a substantive response within ten working days. These are service targets, not a limit on your rights. If the issue needs longer, I will explain why and give an update date. I will consider the agreement, evidence and any remedy fairly. If you disagree with the response, you can ask for reconsideration with any further evidence.

Escalation and legal rights

A complaint does not prevent you using available statutory remedies, seeking independent advice or bringing a claim in an appropriate court. Marketplace work may also have a platform dispute route. Privacy complaints can be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office. I do not claim membership of an alternative dispute-resolution scheme on this page. Where an unresolved consumer dispute requires ADR information to be supplied, that information and whether I will participate will be provided as required.
